title: File:Confederate 100 Dollars.jpg

ObjectName.value: Confederate 100 Dollars

Categories.value: PD US|Images with annotations|Author died more than 100 years ago public domain images|Photographs by User:Swtpc6800|Featured pictures on Wikipedia, Persian|Featured pictures on Wikipedia, Turkish|CC-PD-Mark|1862 banknotes|100 dollar Confederate banknotes|Featured pictures in the public domain|Plants on banknotes|Ceres on banknotes|Slaves on banknotes|Featured pictures of banknotes

ImageDescription.value:
A One Hundred Dollar Confederate States of America banknote dated December 22, 1862. Issued during the American Civil War (1861–1865).

Slave hoeing cotton in the center with John C. Calhoun on the left and Columbia on the right. Over 670,000 of these notes were issued from August, 1862 to January, 1863. [1]

The bill is 7.375 by 3.125 inches (187 mm by 79 mm) and is thinner than a modern US dollar.

Annotations on the banknote.

Serial number 131615
Keatinge & Ball, Columbia, S.C. (lower left)
Receivable in Payment of All Dues Except Export Duties. (lower right)
Issued by Maj. James Glover, q.m. 26th January 1863 (hand written on back)
Interest Paid to 1st January 1864 at Richmond. (stamped on back) The ink from this stamp can be seen on the front right side.

title: File:A mosaic located along Boston's Freedom Trail commemorating the site of the first public school, the Latin School. (b6a5b6e4-2737-4810-9f27-8d1cec8a1e8e).JPG

ObjectName.value: First School Mosaic

Categories.value: PD US NPS|Images from NPGallery to check|Media needing category review with 1 suggested category|Photographs taken on 2018-05-15|Images from NPGallery|Media needing category review as of 15 January 2022|Boston Latin School mosaic

ImageDescription.value:
This image is of a mosaic set into the ground to commemorate the site of the first public school, the Latin School. The mosaic is shaped like an arch. In the top circle, there is a depiction of the school in red and peach. The name Latin School is below that in gold. Under that are three paragraphs of text that are too small to read. Below that is a depiction of children playing old style games like hoops, kite flying, and jump rope. Around this along the border is an alphabet of the letters plus a tile showing an animal or item that starts with that letter. Around that is a splay of red bricks.

A mosaic located along Boston's Freedom Trail commemorating the site of the first public school, the Latin School.

title: File:Boston Common (7194230690).jpg

ObjectName.value: Boston Common (7194230690)

Categories.value: Taken with Nikon D5000|State Street Bank|Flickr images reviewed by File Upload Bot (Magnus Manske)|May 2012 in Boston|Files from InSapphoWeTrust Flickr stream|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Boston Common in the 2010s

ImageDescription.value:
In the Boston area, urban planning often followed that of 17th Century England, where the settlers hailed from. Boston Common is one such feature; in English towns, a "common" is a common area of land that the residents could use on a communal basis for agricultural, grazing, and other uses. Boston Common has the distinction of being America's oldest urban park, dating back to 1634.

Boston Common is also the southern terminus of the Freedom Trail, which meanders through downtown to connect various historical points of interest. Its northern terminus is across the Charles River at Bunker Hill. The trail is marked with red bricks (as seen here) or with a red painted line.
